# Pre-publish leak-check fixture -- see CLAUDE.md 'The pre-publish check'.
#
# Ten lines. The first six MUST be caught by the check's pattern: its four classes, plus the
# second separator of the drive class -- the pattern accepts \ or /, and only \ was shown,
# so / was covered by the code and by nothing else (2026-09-03). The last four MUST NOT be
# caught, and they are the half that matters -- two earlier drafts of the pattern were wrong
# precisely because they tripped on safe text (T-013). The forward-slash near-miss is the
# URL below, which must stay ignored. Every path here is fabricated: this file is evidence,
# not a record of anyone's machine.

drive Q:\Projects\example                <- must be caught
home /home/someone/project               <- must be caught
users /Users/someone/project             <- must be caught
unc \\fileserver\share\docs              <- must be caught
ip 192.0.2.42                            <- must be caught
slash Q:/Projects/example                <- must be caught

safe https://example.com/a               <- must be ignored
safe a python d:\n escape in a string    <- must be ignored
safe the words drive letters, hostnames  <- must be ignored
safe version 1.2.3 and a range 1-3       <- must be ignored
